column2: Regarding only partial orders are getting manifested.
column3: Regarding only partial orders are getting manifested. Denny Quote:  "In the first call, the request contained 11 order codes, and the call failed. During the retry, the second request contained 21 order codes, after which the call succeeded. However, only the initial 11 order codes present in the first request were manifested. Because of this, we see a discrepancy: the manifest is marked as done in corehouse, but the manifest is unsuccessful in increff and marketplace for remaining orders. Please ensure that when retrying the manifest_handover call, you do not add or remove any order codes from the original request payload." GB reply: This API behavior was not communicated during the initial integration discussion/documentation. From our understanding, whenever we receive a 200 OK response, we treat the entire request as successful for all order codes included in that payload. In this scenario, during the retry call, the request contained 21 order codes and the API returned a successful response. If only the original 11 order codes were actually manifested and the remaining 10 failed, then ideally the complete request should not have been marked as successful. This indicates a flaw or inconsistency in the API behavior/response handling at your end, as the response did not clearly communicate partial success or failure for individual order codes. We have implemented solution for this due to its urgency. I need confirmation if all latest orders are successfully marked completed at assure side or not.

Regarding label format. Quote by Huzaifa: "For shipping labels for marketplaces : Label Size Standards: Common Standard: Most systems support 4 × 6 inches (102 × 152 mm) — the universal thermal label size accepted by major carriers and shipping platforms. Exception (Flipkart): Certain Flipkart flows use 3 × 5 inches (76 × 127 mm) under the new label format. Recommendation:   For standardization, use 4 × 6 inches as your default thermal label size — it ensures compatibility across most systems. For Flipkart-specific shipments, verify 3 × 5 inches label compatibility where applicable. For invoice and shipping label formats, the files are generally available in PDF format. However, in the case of Amazon, the shipping label is originally generated in ZPL format, which is then converted to PDF for easier viewing and printing compatibility." Our repy: "The earlier communication mentioned that, for Amazon shipments, the shipping label is originally generated in ZPL format and then converted to PDF for easier viewing and printing compatibility. Based on that statement, the expectation was that the OMS would handle the ZPL-to-PDF conversion before exposing the label downstream. However, we are still receiving the label in raw ZPL format instead of PDF."
